newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga to invest 1.2 bln rgt for projects.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga to invest 1.2 bln rgt for projects.

text.p: National electricity company Tenaga Nasional Bhd said on Friday it has to invest an estimated 1.2 billion ringgit over two years to supply power to 12 huge infrastructure projects in Malaysia.
"We estimate that the investment will have to be made over two years," said Tenaga executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali. "Our projects have to be carried out before the actual projects," he added.
Tajuddin was speaking to reporters after awarding a 36 million ringgit contract to build two power substations to Arab Malaysian Best & Crompton, a subsidiary of Arab Malaysian Development Bhd.

He said the 12 infrastructure projects were the 9.0 billion ringgit Kuala Lumpur International Airport; the Kuala Lumpur City Centre, which features the world's tallest buildings in the Petronas Towers, and phase one and two of the Light Rail Transit in Kuala Lumpur.

The other projects are Plaza Rakyat, a commercial complex in the capital; commercial developments Sentul Raya and MidValley City; the National Sports Complex; Berjaya Star City; Plaza Merdeka, Linear City, a riverside development featuring the world's longest building and Sentral Kuala Lumpur, a complex of office towers and condominiums.

Asked if Tenaga would needed to raise additional funds for these projects, Tajuddin said: "We have our own capital expenditure programme on how we intend to finance these projects. We do have enough for the moment."
But Tajuddin added the company would raise funds as and when it needed for its various operations and projects.
"We have to go to the capital market and we may be announcing it soon," he said.
